les: Hoe 'n vuur begin, en hoe jy veilig bly
kaps_punt: brandstof benodig hitte om hulle aan die brand te gesteek, en lug (suurstof) om die brand proses te onderhou; vure is 'n gevaar in ons gemeenskappe

items.bewering: Droë hout lê op 'n hoop en brand nie vanself nie. ... Brandstof moet eers warm genoeg word voordat dit aan die brand slaan. 'n Vuurhoutjie, 'n aansteker of 'n vonk gee vir die hout daardie eerste hitte.
items.blok: Hoe 'n vuur begin
items.bron: Wood-ignition literature (CFI Trainer, 2005 CCAI 'Wood ignition'; UMD DRUM 'Radiant Auto-Ignition of Wood'): a wood fire starts when an external heat source raises the surface temperature to the point of pyrolysis and ignition; piloted ignition at roughly 210-497 C. A heap of dry firewood at ordinary temperatures does not ignite on its own.

items.bewering: Die energie is reeds in die hout gestoor.
items.blok: Hoe 'n vuur begin
items.bron: I'm a Scientist (archive.imascientist.org.uk) and ScienceABC 'What happens to wood when it burns': burning releases chemical energy stored in the wood as heat and light, in an exothermic reaction with oxygen. Strictly the energy belongs to the wood-and-oxygen reaction; 'stored in the fuel' is the standard school framing and not false at this level.

items.bewering: Daardie eerste hitte steek die vuur net aan. Die hitte wat die hout so aansteek, is die insetenergie.
items.blok: Hoe 'n vuur begin
items.bron: Same wood-ignition sources (the external heat only starts ignition, after which combustion carries on) together with the lesson's own definition of 'inset'; the input/output labelling is a consistent use of the terms and not a factual claim that could be wrong.

items.bewering: Jy hoef nie die vuurhoutjie heeltyd by die hout te hou nie. Die vuur maak daarna self genoeg hitte om aan te hou brand. Daardie hitte steek die stuk hout langsaan ook aan die brand.
items.blok: Die vuur maak sy eie hitte
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle' (combustion is exothermic and gives off enough heat to keep itself going); wildland fire-behaviour training material (hunter-ed.com 'Wind effects', Nova Scotia Basic Forest Fire Suppression Course): radiant and convective heat from flames pre-heats and ignites neighbouring unburnt fuel.

items.bewering: Die hitte en die lig uit die vuur is die uitsetenergie.
items.blok: Die vuur maak sy eie hitte
items.bron: I'm a Scientist / ScienceABC: burning wood turns chemical energy into heat and light. Calling these the output energy matches the lesson's definition of 'uitset'.

items.bewering: Byna al daardie hitte en lig kom uit die energie wat in die hout gestoor was. Die res kom van die vuurhoutjie se eerste bietjie hitte.
items.blok: Die vuur maak sy eie hitte
items.bron: Conservation of energy (I'm a Scientist): the output is the energy released by the fuel plus the small input that started it. A match's heat is tiny next to a burning wood fire, so 'byna al' is the right quantifier and is neither too strong nor too weak.

items.bewering: Water op 'n houtvuur vat die brandende hout se hitte weg, en die vuur gaan dood.
items.blok: Die vuur maak sy eie hitte
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle': water takes heat away as it heats up and evaporates, cooling the burning material below the temperature at which it keeps burning. The lesson says this about a wood fire only, where it holds; it does not extend it to oil or electrical fires.

items.bewering: 'n Vuur het ook lug nodig om aan die brand te bly. Dit is die suurstof in die lug wat die vuur gebruik.
items.blok: Lug hou die vuur aan die gang
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle': oxygen, normally from the air, is one of the three things a fire needs; cutting off air puts it out.

items.bewering: Wanneer wind oor 'n houtvuur waai, kry die vuur nuwe lug. Die vlamme brand dan sterker.
items.blok: Lug hou die vuur aan die gang
items.bron: hunter-ed.com prescribed-burn study guide 'Wind effects' and the Nova Scotia Basic Forest Fire Suppression Course (Lesson 3, wind): wind brings a continuous supply of oxygen to the fire and makes it burn more intensely. (Wind also tilts flames onto new fuel; the lesson leaves that out but does not say anything false.)

items.bewering: 'n Glas oor 'n brandende kers hou nuwe lug uit. Die vlam word kleiner en gaan dood wanneer daar nie genoeg suurstof oorbly nie.
items.blok: Lug hou die vuur aan die gang
items.bron: UBC 'Candle in the Jar Debrief' handout and STAO 'Candle under glass experiment': the flame shrinks and goes out once oxygen falls below the level needed to keep burning, not when all the oxygen is used up. The wording 'nie genoeg suurstof oorbly nie' avoids the common 'all the oxygen is used' misconception, which is correct.

items.bewering: 'n Vuur brand net wanneer brandstof, hitte en suurstof bymekaar is. Vat een van die drie weg en die vuur gaan dood. Water op 'n houtvuur vat die hitte weg, en 'n glas oor die kers hou die lug weg.
items.blok: Al drie tegelyk
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle'; NC Office of the State Fire Marshal 'Grade 2 fire triangle' (ncosfm.gov); hardhattraining.com 'What are the 3 methods for extinguishing a fire': taking away heat, fuel or oxygen puts a fire out; water mainly takes away heat, and smothering takes away air. The fire-triangle model: I checked the mapping, and both of the lesson's examples sit on the correct side. A learner who reasons further will not be misled at this level. (The 'fire tetrahedron' adds the chain reaction, which is outside Grade 5.)

items.bewering: Dieselfde drie dinge wys ook hoe 'n mens 'n brand kan keer.
items.blok: Al drie tegelyk
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle': fire prevention and putting fires out both rest on keeping the three elements apart or taking one away.

items.bewering: Vure is 'n gevaar in ons gemeenskappe. 'n Kers, 'n paraffienlamp of 'n stofie val om en steek 'n gordyn of 'n kombers aan.
items.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
items.bron: MDPI Fire 4(3):39 'Towards Understanding Fire Causes in Informal Settlements Based on Inhabitant Risk Perception' (doi 10.3390/fire4030039) and the Royal Academy of Engineering EngX study comparing Dhaka and Cape Town: open flames (candles, paraffin lamps and stoves) are the main known cause of fires in South African informal settlements; Childsafe Cape Town names fallen candles and paraffin as the two main causes of shack fires. Western Cape Government (westerncape.gov.za gc-news 33/5818): keep stoves on a flat surface, away from things that can burn.

items.bewering: 'n Brand begin ook wanneer iemand 'n vlam of kos op die stoof alleen laat.
items.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
items.bron: City of Cape Town media release 'Residents urged not to leave open flames unattended to reduce fire risk' (capetown.gov.za): watch open flames closely while cooking and never leave a flame or fire unattended; Western Cape Government: fires and cooking stoves should never be left unattended.

items.bewering: Klein kinders kry vuurhoutjies of 'n aansteker in die hande en speel daarmee.
items.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
items.bron: City of Cape Town fire safety tips (reported by Weekend Argus / Cape Argus): children should be encouraged not to play with matches or lighters, and these should be stored where children cannot reach them. MDPI Fire 4(3):39: unattended flames within reach of young children are a cause of fires.

items.bewering: 'n Stukkende draad of 'n oorlaaide prop word warm en kan aan die brand slaan.
items.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
items.bron: Cornwall Council Fire and Rescue 'Electrical fire safety' and Essex Fire and Rescue incident reports ('Overloaded socket causes bedroom fire'): too much current makes plugs, leads and sockets hot enough to melt insulation and start a fire. MDPI Fire 4(3):39: electrical faults are the next most common cause after open flames in South African informal settlements, often through substandard wiring.

items.bewering: In elkeen van hierdie gevalle bereik hitte 'n brandstof.
items.blok: Hoe brande in ons gemeenskappe begin
items.bron: Checked against each of the four cases in the block (fallen flame onto fabric, unattended flame or food, matches, hot wire or plug), using the fire-triangle sources above: in every case a heat source reaches something that burns, with air already present. The generalisation holds for every item in the list.

items.bewering: Die meeste reëls wat 'n brand keer, hou een van die drie dinge weg van die ander twee.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n brand keer
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle' (prevention by keeping the elements apart), checked against the rules the block itself gives and the City of Cape Town tips: candles, matches and stoves are all about keeping a heat source away from things that burn. The block names its own exceptions honestly (the stove, where the three are together on purpose; the plug rule, which stops heat from arising). 'Die meeste' is therefore the correct quantifier, not 'alle'.

items.bewering: Sit 'n kers in 'n swaar houer wat nie maklik omval nie, en hou dit weg van gordyne en beddegoed.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n brand keer
items.bron: City of Cape Town tips: make sure candles are secure and cannot fall over (e.g. in a container of sand). NFPA-based candle guidance as repeated by Seattle Fire Department 'Fireline' and Warwickshire County Council 'Fire safety around candles': sturdy holders that won't tip over, and at least about 30 cm away from curtains, bedding and other things that can burn.

items.bewering: Bêre vuurhoutjies en aanstekers hoog op waar klein kinders nie kan bykom nie.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n brand keer
items.bron: City of Cape Town fire safety tips: matches and lighters should be stored in a safe place where children cannot reach them.

items.bewering: Los nooit 'n vlam of kos op die stoof alleen nie. By die stoof is die drie dinge met opset bymekaar. Iemand moet daar wees om 'n klein vuur betyds te blus.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n brand keer
items.bron: City of Cape Town 'Residents urged not to leave open flames unattended'; Western Cape Government: cooking stoves should never be left unattended. That the three elements are together on purpose on a cooking flame is consistent with the fire-triangle sources.

items.bewering: Moenie te veel proppe by een muurprop insteek nie, want die draad word warm. Daardie reël keer dat die hitte ontstaan.
items.blok: Hoe jy 'n brand keer
items.bron: City of Cape Town: do not overload power points. Which? 'How to avoid overloading your plug sockets at home' and Cornwall Fire and Rescue: too many appliances on one socket draws too much current, and that heats the plug, lead and wiring.

items.bewering: Skreeu hard sodat almal in die huis weet daar is 'n brand. / Gaan dadelik by die naaste veilige deur uit en bly buite.
items.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
items.bron: Cheshire Fire and Rescue 'In the event of a fire' (cheshirefire.gov.uk): warn everyone, get out, stay out. Nationwide Children's Hospital 'Fire Safety for Children': leave at once, get out and stay out.

items.bewering: Moenie wegkruip nie en moenie vir speelgoed of klere teruggaan nie.
items.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital 'Fire Safety for Children'; University of Kentucky HealthCare 'Tips in preparing children to escape fire'; CBS Colorado ('Firefighters: children hiding during house fires common'): children often hide under beds or in cupboards, which stops firefighters finding them; teach them never to hide and never to go back inside for anything.

items.bewering: Rook trek boontoe, dus bly jy laag terwyl jy na buite beweeg.
items.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
items.bron: University of Maine emergency guidance (umaine.edu/alert) and the University of Rhode Island 'Fire Safety Tips': heavy smoke and poisonous gases collect first along the ceiling, so the air is cleaner low down; crawl or stay low.

items.bewering: As jy kan, trek die deur agter jou toe, want dit hou die vuur terug.
items.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
items.bron: Cheshire Fire and Rescue and Devon and Somerset Fire and Rescue (dsfire.gov.uk): close doors behind you if you can, because a closed door slows the spread of fire and smoke.

items.bewering: As jou klere brand, staan stil en gaan op die grond lê. / Bedek jou gesig met jou hande en rol tot die vlamme dood is.
items.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
items.bron: University of Maine emergency guidance and Cheshire Fire and Rescue: stop (do not run, because running fans the flames), drop to the ground, cover your face with your hands and roll until the flames are out. Both items match stop, drop and roll in order and in content.

items.bewering: Laat 'n grootmens dadelik om hulp bel sodra almal buite is.
items.blok: Wat om te doen tydens 'n brand
items.bron: Howard County MD Emergency Management 'Home fires' and Nationwide Children's Hospital: call the emergency services once you are outside. That an adult phones is a safety choice and not a fact claim; it contains nothing false. (I am noting this only for the person reading the report: the item does not say what a child does if no adult is there. This is not a fact finding.)

items.bewering: brandstof: Iets wat kan brand en dan sy gestoorde energie afgee.
items.blok: brandstof
items.bron: I'm a Scientist / ScienceABC: a fuel releases stored chemical energy when it burns. The definition is simple and correct, and it also holds when read on its own.

items.bewering: suurstof: Die gas in die lug wat 'n vuur gebruik om te brand.
items.blok: suurstof
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fire triangle': the oxidiser in ordinary fires is oxygen in the air. The definition does not claim oxygen is the only gas in air, so it is not too broad.

items.bewering: inset: Die energie wat ingaan om iets te laat werk of gebeur.
items.blok: inset
items.bron: Standard meaning of input energy in a simple energy system (I'm a Scientist, energy transfer). The definition is accurate at this level.

items.bewering: uitset: Al die energie wat uitkom wanneer iets werk of gebeur.
items.blok: uitset
items.bron: Standard meaning of output energy (I'm a Scientist, conservation of energy: energy is redistributed, not lost). 'Al' is not too strong for the whole output, useful and wasted together.

items.bewering: paraffienlamp: 'n Lamp wat lig gee deur paraffien in 'n pit te brand.
items.blok: paraffienlamp
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Kerosene lamp' and EngineerFix 'What is a kerosene lamp and how does it work': the wick draws paraffin (kerosene) up from the reservoir and the fuel burns at its tip, giving light. 'Paraffin' is the South African and British name for kerosene. Pressure lamps with a mantle exist, but the common household lamp has a wick, so the definition is correct.

items.bewering: brandveiligheid: Die maniere waarop mense brande keer en veilig bly as een uitbreek.
items.blok: brandveiligheid
items.bron: Matches the scope of fire-safety guidance from the City of Cape Town and Cheshire Fire and Rescue: prevention, and what to do in a fire. The definition is accurate.

opsomming: All 34 checkable claims are supported. That covers the two quantifiers ('byna al' and 'die meeste reëls'), the fire-triangle model and its two examples, the South African causes of fires, the prevention rules and the steps to take in a fire. There is no comparison in the lesson apart from the fire triangle, and its mapping holds; nothing needs fixing, and the only thing a person might want to look at is a choice rather than a fact: the last list item has an adult phone for help and does not say what a child does without one.
